name: Prasugrel
dosing: Loading 60mg, then 10mg daily (consider 5mg daily in elderly/low body weight per guidance); used per ACS/PCI protocols
contraindications: Prior history of stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA), active pathological bleeding, severe hepatic impairment
interactions: Concomitant antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy increases bleeding risk; avoid with other agents that significantly increase bleeding unless specifically indicated
monitoring: Monitor for signs of bleeding, haemoglobin and platelet count where clinically indicated; assess renal and hepatic function as relevant
pregnancy: Use only if benefits justify potential risks; specialist/cardiology advice required
sideEffects: Bleeding is the principal adverse effect (including major bleeding); bruising and minor bleeding are common
clinicalPearls: Preferred P2Y12 inhibitor in some PCI/ACS settings for patients at lower bleeding risk; consider dose reduction (5 mg) in elderly (>75) or low body weight per guidance; avoid in prior stroke/TIA patients
indication: Antiplatelet therapy in acute coronary syndrome particularly in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (follow cardiology protocols)
